title: Energy, Energy Transfer & General Energy Analysis

questions.prompt: What distinguishes **heat** from **work** as an energy transfer?
choices: Heat is driven by a temperature difference; work is any other organized transfer
Heat is stored in the system; work is not
Work is always larger than heat
Heat crosses the boundary; work does not
questions.explanation: Both cross the boundary, and neither is stored — the defining feature of heat is that a temperature difference drives it; everything else (shaft, electrical, boundary movement) is work.

questions.prompt: A process is **adiabatic** when…
questions.explanation: Adiabatic means no heat transfer ($Q = 0$). Temperature can still change — e.g. adiabatic compression heats a gas.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a **property** of a system?
questions.explanation: Internal energy is stored by the system and depends only on its state. Heat and work are transfers (path-dependent), and power is a transfer rate.

questions.prompt: A system **loses 5 kJ of heat** and **does 10 kJ of work**. With the convention "$Q$ in +, $W$ out +", what goes into the energy balance?
questions.explanation: Heat *leaving* is negative; work *done by* the system is positive. Then $\Delta E = Q - W = -5 - 10 = -15$ kJ.

questions.prompt: If the wind speed at a turbine site **doubles**, the available wind power is multiplied by…
questions.explanation: Available wind power scales with $V^3$ ($\dot W = \tfrac12\rho A V^3$), so doubling the speed gives $2^3 = 8\times$ the power.

questions.prompt: An electric motor ($\eta = 0.90$) drives a pump ($\eta = 0.70$). The overall electricity-to-fluid efficiency is…
questions.explanation: Chained devices multiply: $\eta_{overall} = 0.90 \times 0.70 = 0.63$. Each stage takes its cut of what the previous one delivers.

questions.prompt: Solve the thermal-efficiency definition $\eta_{th} = W_{net}/Q_H$ for the required heat input $Q_H$:
questions.explanation: Multiply both sides by $Q_H$ and divide by $\eta_{th}$: to get a desired work output you must supply $W_{net}/\eta_{th}$ of heat.

questions.prompt: The kinetic energy **per unit mass** of a flow moving at velocity $V$ is…
questions.explanation: $KE = \tfrac12 mV^2$, so per unit mass $ke = V^2/2$ (in J/kg when $V$ is in m/s).

questions.prompt: The instantaneous **electrical power** drawn by a device at voltage $V$ and current $I$ is…
questions.explanation: Power is $VI$ (watts); multiplying by time $\Delta t$ gives the *energy* $W_e = VI\,\Delta t$ (joules).

questions.prompt: Find the **kinetic energy** of a **1000 kg** car moving at **20 m/s**, in kJ.
A heat engine with thermal efficiency **0.30** receives **1500 kJ** of heat. How much **net work** does it produce?
questions.explanation: $W_{net} = \eta_{th} Q_H = 0.30 \times 1500 = 450$ kJ.

questions.prompt: A **2.0 kW** heater runs for **30 minutes**. How much energy does it deliver, in kJ?
questions.explanation: $W = \dot W \Delta t = 2.0\ \text{kW} \times 1800\ \text{s} = 3600$ kJ — keep time in seconds so kW·s = kJ.

questions.prompt: The **first law of thermodynamics** is essentially a statement of…
questions.explanation: The first law says energy is conserved — it changes form or crosses the boundary, but is never created or destroyed.

questions.prompt: The **mechanical energy** of a flowing fluid ($P/\rho + V^2/2 + gz$) deliberately excludes…
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy is the part fully convertible to work; internal energy is left out because it cannot all be turned into work (second law).

questions.prompt: If wind speed **triples**, the available wind power increases by a factor of…
questions.explanation: Available power scales with $V^3$, so $3^3 = 27$.

questions.prompt: A real pump always needs **more** shaft power than the ideal $\dot m g \Delta z$ because…
choices: Its efficiency is below 1 (friction and other losses)
The ideal value is always wrong
questions.explanation: $\dot W_{shaft} = \dot W_{ideal}/\eta$ with $\eta < 1$, so the real input exceeds the ideal minimum.

questions.prompt: Solve $PE = mgz$ for the **height** $z$:
questions.explanation: Divide both sides by $mg$.

questions.prompt: Solve the shaft-power relation $\dot W_{sh} = 2\pi \dot n\, T$ for the **torque** $T$:
questions.explanation: Divide by $2\pi \dot n$ (with $\dot n$ in rev/s).

questions.prompt: Find the **potential energy** gained when a 200 kg load is lifted 10 m ($g = 9.81\ \text{m/s}^2$), in kJ.
A hydro plant has $\dot m = 300\ \text{kg/s}$, head **60 m**, and overall efficiency **0.80** ($g = 9.81$). Find the electric power, in kW.
questions.explanation: $\dot W = \eta\, \dot m g \Delta z = 0.80 \times 300 \times 9.81 \times 60 = 141\,264$ W $\approx 141.3$ kW.
